items.title: Wonders of Mawrth
items.description: Often appearing as a candidate landing site, Mawrth Vallis is a topographical wonderland of inverted channels, light-toned rocks and clays. Clay minerals have implications for past wet environments along with the potential to preserve biosignatures. This public request was made to investigate the regional stratigraphy and reasons for the topographic inversion.

items.title: New view of NGC 4394 raises the bar
Dunes of Meridiani Planum
items.description: This observation shows really nice, well-spaced barchan and dome dunes that were visible in a 2008 image. In 2014, we detected changes with another picture of the same area. With a stereo pair and a digital terrain model, we can better quantify the sand flux.

items.title: Dust In Cassiopeia A (MIRI Image)
items.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reveals the hot dust that makes up Cassiopeia A. The composition of its dust provides clues to the structure of Cassiopeia A’s original star.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Tea Temim (Columbia University), Rick Arendt (UMBC), Dan Milisavljevic (Purdue University); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Cutting through History
items.description: In this image, we see a portion of Cerberus Fossae cutting hills that predate volcanic flooding. With this observation, we can take another high resolution look at previously exposed stratigraphy. There might be a be a nice stack of ancient lavas.

items.title: A Patchy Outcrop of Light-Toned Materials
items.description: This observation targets patchy exposures of light-toned outcrops. These materials may be chloride bearing. Erosion appears to have cut through the entirety of the light-toned materials, which should allow probing of the stratigraphic context, thickness and any possible internal layering of these materials.

items.title: Curiosity Spots Drifting Twilight Clouds
items.description: NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured these drifting clouds on Oct. 31, 2026, the 5,061st Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The rover uses its navigation cameras to capture post-sunset clouds, called twilight clouds, which appear for only a short time each fall over Gale Crater, which it has been exploring for more than …

items.title: Dust Devil Tracks on Bright Dunes
items.description: This image features dark dust devil tracks on bright dunes that have an odd distribution. The dunes look wind eroded: striations or layering? A false color contrast between dunes and dust devil tracks may provide information to understand dune formation, shape, and dust devil initiation. This footprint is in Galle Crater.

items.title: Troughs and Ridges
items.description: This image features a wide trough with a narrow ridge running down the middle. How did these form? This scene is in Chryse Planitia, a flat lowland region in the Northern Hemisphere of Mars that was chosen for the landing sites for Viking 1 and Mars Pathfinder. The region shows evidence of water erosion in the past.

items.title: Fractured in Elysium
items.description: Researchers suspect this crater’s fractured floor is related to invasive lava, and it resembles weird tilted-facet terrain elsewhere on Mars. A stereo pair along some coverage of the lava outside the crater rim can help us determine how the elevations compare.

items.title: A Ridge Runs through It
items.description: Also visible in a Context Camera image, our objective for this observation is to determine the nature of this long ridge to the northeast of Huygens Crater, itself to the west of the massive Hellas impact basin. The ridge is mostly straight, and it might be a dike, but is unlikely to be volcanic in origin.

items.title: A Collage Showing 49 Drill Holes Made by NASA’s Curiosity Mars Rover
items.description: This collage shows 49 drill holes captured by NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover as of November 2026. Each hole represents a sample collected from rocks on the Martian surface; Curiosity’s drill, located on the end of its robotic arm, drops pulverized rock samples into instruments in its belly that analyze their composition. These images were …

items.title: Tales of a Sinuous Ridge
items.description: This previously unidentified sinuous ridge from a recent global survey is part of a follow-up to test for a possible fluvial origin and determine the depositional setting of previously unmapped ridges across Mars. Identifying these types of fluvial ridges outside of craters is key for reconstructing ancient sedimentary basins as well learning about the past climate.

items.title: Ridges and Channels in Memnonia Sulci
items.description: These ridges and channels in Memnonia Sulci may be part of a fan complex on the dichotomy boundary of Amazonis Planitia and Terra Sirenum. This target was requested to deduce the history of fluvial activity in the region and the relationship of the fans to the Medusa Fossae Formation to the east of here.

items.title: A Light-Toned Exposure in Tyrrhena Terra
items.description: The objective of this observation is to determine the nature of an exposure of light-toned material. This material appears in different spots in a Context Camera image. This picture is one of the most intense spots: that is, it shows quite a contrast with the surrounding ground. Pictures like these may be combined with CRISM data to better understand what is going on in this region.

items.title: Crisp Changes
items.description: This stunning observation features a morphologically crisp, large dune to the east of central peak in an impact crater. The dune has potentially active seasonal mass wasting processes that we can attempt to track over time. The bright patches are exposed frost and the spots are results of where the frost has sublimed away.

items.title: A Ridge in Claritas Fossae
items.description: From HiWish: “This image covers a ridge in Claritas Fossae that seems to be superposed on the older fractures and that is a part of a more numerous assemblage of similarly looking edifices within this region. We propose that this ridge might be volcanic in origin and by using the HiRISE, we can observe details that might support or disprove such claim.”

items.title: Exploring Coprates Chasma
items.description: Light toned material has been observed by the Context Camera and potentially reflects low-calcium pyroxene that indicates pristine crustal material exposed in this location. This is an area of interest for a potential future rotorcraft mission traverse (Mars Science Helicopter) that would explore this and other terrains in situ.

items.title: Northern Plains Flow Features
items.description: This observation shows features that look like a flow margin around a kipuka, so this is definitely worth a closer look. A “kipuka”, a Hawaiian term, is an area of land that is surrounded by younger lava flows, in effect an “island” within a sea of lava.

items.title: Of Rocky Deposits
items.description: This observation features polygonal cracks that may be the remnants of an ancient lake bed. Our image will also fill in a gap in mosaic coverage of this area, a large impact crater at the edge of Isidis Planitia, in the North Hemisphere of Mars.

items.title: Sinuous Ridges and Possible Layers
items.description: A Context Camera image shows sinuous ridges and possible layers at this location, which is within an alluvial-fan-bearing crater. One possible interpretation is that erosion has formed inverted channels and incised them into distal alluvial fan or deltaic materials. A derived 3D image can help look for “double ridges” that might be bracketing inverted channels.

items.title: Esker Candidates in Mamers Valles
items.description: An esker is a long ridge of sediment deposited by meltwater from a retreating glacier or ice sheet. Although glaciers are common on Mars, in the prevailing very cold and dry climate they are thought to be almost exclusively cold-based systems, which do not experience subglacial melt. These candidate eskers could be important to our understanding of non-climatic drivers of meltwater production…

items.title: Layers to the West of Gale Crater
items.description: The objective of this observation is to examine thin layers in the Nepenthes Mensae region. Because this location is close to Gale Crater, these layers may one day be compared to those currently being studied by the Curiosity rover. Nepenthes Mensae is a plateau, whose name derives from Greek for a drug that quells all sorrows with forgetfulness and is mentioned in Homer’s “Odyssey.”

items.title: The Beauty of Inverted Channels
items.description: This observation was public suggestion from HiWish: to image an area within an eroded impact crater that shows very clear layers and inverted channels exposed in the distal ends of two alluvial fans. Inverted channels are made from deposits that wind up being more resistant to erosion than the surrounding terrain and so remain higher-standing.

items.title: Layering and Cross-Cutting Bands
items.description: This mound exhibits layering and cross-cutting bands that correspond to an iron/magnesium phyllosilicate composition elsewhere in mounds in Chryse Planitia. This particular mesa has a large surface area and excellent exposure, which is ideal for observations of stratigraphic relationships.

items.title: Irregular Circular Depressions around Naar Crater
items.description: Our objective is to analyze a new unknown feature dubbed “irregular circular depressions.” The features are located directly on the outer rim of the crater. This image is of geologic interest since their origin is unknown: could they be related to impact cratering or perhaps due to the presence of ice?

items.title: A Lava Flow near the Elysium Rise
items.description: This image is of the perimeter of a lava flow found on the western slope of the Elysium volcanic region. Elysium Mons is the largest of the three volcanoes centered on this region, towering some 16 kilometers (52,500 feet) above the surrounding plains. Two smaller volcanoes, Albor Tholus to the south and Hecates Tholus to the north, also lie within this vast region ( see map ). The lava flow in…

items.title: Dwarf Galaxy NGC 4449
items.description: This is an image from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope of NGC 4449, one of the dwarf galaxies in the Galaxies Losing Oxygen via Winds (GLOW) study. Researchers found that dwarf galaxies can hold onto only a small fraction of the oxygen made by their stars.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, Hubble Heritage–ESA/Hubble Collaboration, Alessandra Aloisi (STScI, ESA)

items.title: Impact-Related Flows in Margaritifer Terra
items.description: Our rationale for acquiring this image it to observe how the surface flow patterns in the area vary with distance from the crater. This is one of several flow feature observations suggested in the vicinity of the well-preserved crater to the south. Margaritifer Terra is centered just south of the Martian equator and with chaotic terrain, outflow channels and alluvial plains.

items.title: Well-Preserved Polygons
items.description: Polygons are interesting features on Mars, though sometimes only visible in high resolution images like those taken by HiRISE. They often form due to the contraction and expansion of ice under the surface. These polygons, in Elysium Planitia and to the east of Apollinaris Patera, are unusually well-preserved, so we can take a more detailed look at their textures with this observation.

items.title: Ancient Bedrock in the Southern Highlands
items.description: This image of an ancient rocky hill in the Southern Highlands proved to be surprisingly colorful due to diverse rock compositions. In this color cutout , the bluish and greenish rocks are probably unaltered rocks rich in pyroxenes and olivine, whereas the warmer tones may be from minerals altered by water.

items.title: Ancient Layers Exposed by a Crater within a Crater
items.description: Terra Sirenum is a heavily cratered region of Mars’ ancient Southern Highlands. A blanket of dust, possibly cemented by ice, covers much of the ancient bedrock in these Martian middle latitudes, but impacts can expose buried materials in the resulting steep crater walls. Here, a roughly 2-kilometer diameter crater reveals light-toned layered material on the floor of a much larger, infilled…

items.title: Cat’s Head Nebula (Hubble WFC3 Image)
items.description: NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope shows an opaque dust pillar edged by a luminous rim of gas. Surrounding blue regions include emission from ionized gas and scattered starlight. The cat’s glowing red eye may indicate a young star embedded in the dust.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Glacial and Periglacial Terrains
items.description: This image will help define the fine-grained shapes of a glacial terrain just east of a periglacial mantle that appeared in earlier HiRISE observation. The periglacial terrain lays on top of a mantle that may retain the cratering history of the region. We also can constrain the age of the area.

items.title: Light and Dark Dunes in Nili Fossae
items.description: Our science goal with this observation is one of monitoring these odd, light-colored dome and barchan dunes on the floor of Nili Fossae, a known high sand flux region. Nili Fossae is a group of large, concentric grabens on Mars, in the Syrtis Major region.

items.title: NASA’s Perseverance Views Dust at Neretva Vallis
items.description: This 360-degree look at Neretva Vallis within Mars’ Jezero Crater was stitched together using 217 images acquired by the rover’s Mastcam-Z on May 20, 2024, the 1,155th Martian day, or sol, of the mission. While it is a wind-swept dusty vista today, billions of years ago it was home to a river channel that fed fresh water into …

items.title: Lava of Cerberus Palus
items.description: When our camera is pointed straight down at the surface of Mars, we call this “nadir.” This particular terrain, featuring platy-ridged lava, loans itself for good nadir images. Cerberus Palus once contained a lake that might have been either water or lava. The large plates almost look like pack ice, and gaps between them contain impressive lava coils that are bigger than ones found on Earth.

During that sol’s drive, spanning 299.6 feet (91.31 meters), the mission passed a major milestone: pushing Perseverance’s total …

items.title: NASA’s Curiosity Looks Back After Reaching Elevation Milestone
items.description: NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured this view looking back at the floor of Gale Crater, with the crater’s rim visible in the distance, on Sept. 5, 2026, the 5,006th Martian day, or sol, of the mission. Just nine days prior, on Aug. 26 (Sol 4,996), Curiosity set a mission milestone by reaching 1 kilometer …

items.title: NASA’s Curiosity Captures Dawn Breaking on Wind-Carved Cliffs
items.description: NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured this panorama of sunrise illuminating distant, wind-carved features called yardangs on Aug. 11, 2026, the 4,982nd Martian day, or sol, of the mission. Scientists are eager to learn more about how the yardang layer formed. Figure A is a crop zooming in on the distant yardangs. Since 2014, Curiosity …

items.title: NGC 7129 (NIRCam Image)
items.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has revealed many protostars and stars within the glowing gases of NGC 7129. Hot, atomic hydrogen gas is shown here in the golden region, while cooler, molecular hydrogen gas, shocked by embedded protostars, is represented in red.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
Perseverance’s View of ‘Turquoise Bay’
items.description: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover used its Mastcam-Z camera to capture this 360-degree panorama of “Turquoise Bay,” a geologic area of interest in the “Margin Unit.” The 818 images used to create the natural-color panorama were captured between Oct. 5 and Oct. 16, 2023, the 933rd to 944th Martian days, or sols, of the mission. …

items.title: A galaxy spinning out of sync
IC 348 (NIRCam Image)
items.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope recently observed IC 348, a star-forming region just 1,000 light-years away from Earth. Webb’s sharp vision revealed tiny brown dwarfs, some just twice Jupiter’s mass, and young stars ejecting powerful jets crashing into surrounding gas and dust.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, Kevin Luhman (PSU), Catarina Alves de Oliveira (ESA), Mahdi Zamani (ESA/Webb)

items.title: Decagon on Saturn’s South Pole (Color)
items.description: Recent NASA Hubble Space Telescope images show the gas giant Saturn and its southern pole, where astronomers have discovered a 10-sided atmospheric wave. Observations show the decagon extends through multiple layers of Saturn’s atmosphere.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, STScI, Agustin Sánchez-Lavega (UPV), Amy Simon (NASA-GSFC), Michael Wong (UC Berkeley); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan

items.title: Striking star clusters and irregular clumps
Perseverance Captures Another Phobos Transit
items.description: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover used its Mastcam-Z camera to capture the silhouette of Phobos, one of the two Martian moons, as it crossed in front of the Sun on Aug. 12, 2026, the 1,948th Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The animation has been tinted to simulate what a human would see if …

items.title: Lion Nebula (NIRCam and MIRI Image)
items.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope imaged the planetary nebula NGC 2392, the Lion Nebula, using the observatory’s NIRCam and MIRI instruments. The central star’s remains are responsible for the nebula’s structure, including a lion face-shaped bubble of ionized gas and dust “mane.”
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Webb opens a Treasure Chest filled with stars

The black background is the result of …

items.description: NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured this sand-capped butte, nicknamed “Miraflores,” estimated to be about 20 feet (6 meters) tall, with its Mast Camera, or Mastcam, on June 11, 2026, the 4,923rd Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The butte was left behind as surrounding rock eroded away over time, deepening the broad valley …

items.description: NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope has provides a detailed view of millions of stars in Andromeda galaxy.

The series begins with the smallest crescent at the center of the of the image as Mars is farthest from the spacecraft, and progressively …

items.title: Curiosity Finds Evidence of an Ancient Sandstorm
items.description: Billions of years ago, an hours-long Martian sandstorm blew so intensely that sand ripples began to climb upon one another as they moved across the surface. These layers of sediment eventually hardened into the multilayered rocks seen in this image, which was taken by NASA’s Curiosity rover on Dec. 12, 2024, the 4,391st Martian …

The bright-colored rocks exposed across the slope, running from middle left to middle right of …

items.title: Perseverance’s Trip to ‘Broom Point’
items.description: This orbital map shows the path NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover took to get to a location the science team has dubbed the “Broom Point member,” a sequence of layered bedrock likely more than 3.9 billion years old. As planned, the rover landed inside Jezero Crater on Feb. 18, 2021. It investigated the crater’s western delta …

items.title: Centaurus A (MIRI Image)
items.description: The mid-infrared view of Centaurus A from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reveals dusty structures and hidden activity within the nearby, active galaxy.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI), Joseph DePasquale (STScI), Macarena Garcia Marin (STScI)

items.title: Centaurus A Crop (NIRCam and MIRI Image)
items.description: In the combined mid- and near-infrared view of Centaurus A, the NIRCam (Near-Infrared Camera) on NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope brings out the galaxy’s dense field of millions of stars.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI), Joseph DePasquale (STScI), Macarena Garcia Marin (STScI)

items.title: FS Tau (Webb Image)
items.description: In infrared light, NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reveals bright protostars in star system FS Tau and a tapestry of background galaxies. FS Tau B, the orange protostar slightly right of center, is thought to be responsible for the orange outflows amid the dusty region.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

Perseverance reached that distance after five years and four months of driving — on …

items.title: Galaxy MXDFz4.4 (Hubble and Webb Image)
items.description: Detailed visible-light images from Hubble reveal that several bursts of younger stars cleared the space in and around galaxy MXDFz4.4. Astronomers have long sought evidence to explain this transition — and Hubble has provided the first example in this time period.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Ilias Goovaerts (STScI), Marc Rafelski (STScI, JHU), Anton Koekemoer (STScI); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: M82 Cigar Galaxy (Webb + Hubble)
items.description: Scientists used NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope to image edge-on starburst galaxy Messier 82 and trace its evolutionary history. This Webb and Hubble composite image includes 16.5 million stars (blue-white), dust grains (red-orange), and ionized hydrogen gas (yellow).
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, Adam Smercina (STScI, Tufts), Thomas Williams (University of Manchester); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Bulge Fossil Fragment Terzan 5 (Webb and Hubble Image)
items.description: New observations from Webb combined with multiple observations from Hubble prove that Terzan 5 is a self-contained, self-enriching stellar system that contains up to four distinct star populations. It orbits within our Milky Way galaxy’s central bulge.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Giorgia Zullo (University of Bologna), Francesco Ferraro (University of Bologna); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Trifid Nebula (Wide Field Camera 3 Image)
items.description: NASA celebrates Hubble’s 36th anniversary with a new image of the Trifid Nebula, a star-forming region it first captured in 1997. The telescope leveraged almost its full operational lifetime to show us changes in the nebula on human time scales with an improved camera.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.description: A pullout shows where the Hubble Space Telescope’s close-up image is located within the wider Trifid Nebula. The image at left was taken by the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile. The color assignments in the images vary based on the filters in the telescopes’ cameras.
items.credit: Image: Rubin Observatory, NASA, ESA, STScI

items.title: NASA’s SPHEREx Mission Maps Water Ice Throughout Cygnus X
items.description: An observation made by NASA’s SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer) shows the chemical signatures of water ice (shown in bright blue) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (orange) in Cygnus X, one of the most active and turbulent regions of star birth in our Milky Way galaxy.

items.title: Exoplanet 29 Cygni b (NIRCam Image)
items.description: Astronomers used NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope to directly image 29 Cygni b, which weighs 15 times Jupiter. They found evidence for heavy chemical elements like carbon and oxygen, which strongly suggests it formed like a planet by accretion within a protoplanetary disk.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, William Balmer (JHU, STScI), Laurent Pueyo (STScI); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Where spiral arms and star formation meet
Saturn (Webb NIRCam and Hubble WFC3/UVIS)
items.description: Complementary views of Saturn from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope and Hubble Space Telescope show a dynamic planet with atmospheric features, orbiting moons, and bright rings.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Amy Simon (NASA-GSFC), Michael Wong (UC Berkeley); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Crab Nebula (2024)
items.description: This 2024 image that NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope captured of the Crab Nebula, paired with its past observations and those of other telescopes, allows astronomers to study how the supernova remnant is expanding and evolving over time.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, STScI, William Blair (JHU); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Fragmentation of Comet C/2025 K1
items.description: This series of images from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope of the fragmenting comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) was taken over the course of three consecutive days: Nov. 8, 9, and 10, 2025. This is the first time Hubble has witnessed a comet so early in the process of breaking up.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, Dennis Bodewits (AU); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: SN 2025pht in NGC 1637
items.description: The main image at left shows a combined Webb and Hubble view of spiral galaxy NGC 1637. Panels at right show a detailed view of a red supergiant star before and after it exploded. Before exploding, it is not visible to Hubble, only to Webb. Hubble shows the glowing aftermath.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Charles Kilpatrick (Northwestern), Aswin Suresh (Northwestern); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: The stellar lifecycle in a nearby spiral
Dark Galaxy CDG-2 Near Perseus Cluster
items.description: The low-surface-brightness galaxy CDG-2, within the dashed red circle at right, is dominated by dark matter and contains only a sparse scattering of stars. The full image from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope is at left
items.credit: NASA, ESA, Dayi Li (UToronto); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Egg Nebula
items.description: NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope reveals the clearest view yet of the Egg Nebula. This structure of gas and dust was created by a dying, Sun-like star. These newest observations, taken with Hubble’s Wide Field Camera 3, include infrared data for the first time.

items.title: COSMOS Field MoM-z14 Galaxy (NIRCam Image)
items.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope shows galaxy MoM-z14 as it appeared in the distant past, only 280 million years after the universe began in the big bang.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Rohan Naidu (MIT); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Astrophysical Anomalies from Hubble’s Archive
items.description: Six previously undiscovered, weird and fascinating astrophysical objects are displayed in this new image from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope. They include three lenses with arcs distorted by gravity, one galactic merger, one ring galaxy, and one galaxy that defied classification.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, David O'Ryan (ESA), Pablo Gómez (ESA), Mahdi Zamani (ESA/Hubble)

items.title: A celebrity cluster in the spotlight
Protostar EC 53 in the Serpens Nebula (NIRCam Image)
items.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope’s 2024 NIRCam image shows protostar EC 53 circled. Researchers using new data from Webb’s MIRI proved that crystalline silicates form in the hottest part of the disk of gas and dust surrounding the star — and may be shot to the system’s edges.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Klaus Pontoppidan (NASA-JPL), Joel Green (STScI); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Helix Nebula (NIRCam)
items.description: This new image of a portion of the Helix Nebula from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope highlights comet-like knots, fierce stellar winds, and layers of gas shed off by a dying star interacting with its surrounding environment.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI)

items.title: Sextans A Context Image (Webb and KPNO)
items.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope’s image of a portion of the nearby Sextans A galaxy is put into context using a ground-based image from the Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory.
items.credit: Image: STScI, NASA, ESA, CSA, KPNO, NSF's NOIRLab, AURA, Elizabeth Tarantino (STScI), Phil Massey (Lowell Obs.), George Jacoby (NSF, AURA), Chris Smith (NSF, AURA); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI), Travis Rector (UAA), Mahdi Zamani (NSF's NOIRLab), Davide De Martin (NSF's NOIRLab)

items.title: Betelgeuse: Effect of Companion Star Wake
items.description: Scientists used NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope to look for evidence of a wake being generated by a companion star orbiting Betelgeuse. The team found a noticeable difference in light shown in the lefthand peak when the companion star was at different points in its orbit.
items.credit: Illustration: NASA, ESA, Elizabeth Wheatley (STScI); Science: Andrea Dupree (CfA)

items.title: Cloud 9, Starless Gas Cloud
items.description: Magenta is radio data from the ground-based Very Large Array (VLA) showing the presence of Cloud-9. The dashed circle marks area where researchers focused their search for stars. Hubble found no stars within Cloud-9. The few objects within its boundaries are background galaxies.
items.credit: Science: NASA, ESA, VLA, Gagandeep Anand (STScI), Alejandro Benitez-Llambay (University of Milano-Bicocca); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: A neighbouring vista of stellar birth
Dracula’s Chivito (IRAS 23077+6707)
items.description: This Hubble Space Telescope image shows the largest planet-forming disk ever observed around a young star. It spans nearly 400 billion miles — 40 times the diameter of our solar system.

items.title: Dwarf stars in a glittering sky
Fomalhaut cs2
items.description: This composite Hubble Space Telescope image shows the debris ring and dust clouds cs1 and cs2 around the star Fomalhaut. Fomalhaut itself is masked out to allow the fainter features to be seen. Its location is marked by the white star.
items.credit: Image: NASA, ESA, Paul Kalas (UC Berkeley); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

items.title: Finding star clusters in the Lost Galaxy
